To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
optogenetic photo-stimulation of VIP-cre and PV-cre neurons in mouse somato sensory cortex does not produce significant changes in local cerebral blood flow.

the optogenetic activation of NOS and SOM neurons increases CBF in the mouse somatosensory cortex, while the photo-stimulation of PV and VIP inhibitory neurons does not consistently increase CBF in this brain region.

“We found that the activity of specific inhibitory neurons, such as somatostatin, NOS and parvalbumin neurons, can have a significant and different impact on cerebral blood flow regulation, suggesting that dysfunction in these neurons can have a major impact on brain function and disease”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of inhibitory neuronal activity and CBF regulation in mouse somatosensory cortex.
the development of optogenetic techniques for assessing the role of inhibitory neurons on cerebral blood flow regulation.
understanding the relationship between inhibitory neuron activity in mouse somatosensory cortex and the regulation of CBR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optogenetic activation of VIP neurons did not significantly change CBF in the mouse somato-sensor cortex, while optogenetic activation in PV, NOS and SOM neurons produced significant CBF changes.
the role of VIP, PV or SOM neurons on CBF regulation is still unclear and requires further investigation.

optogenetic activation of VIP, SOM and NPS neurons in mouse cortex produces a complex pattern of CBF responses that are not consistent across different neuronal types and are not always detectable in non-transgenic controls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activity of VIP and SOM neurons can have significant impact on the regulation of local cerebral blood flow.
the optogenetic activation of NOS-cre and SOM-cre neurons produced significant increases in cerebral blood flow (i.e., CBF) in mouse somato sensory cortex.

NOS neurons have an excitatory role in CBF responses, SOM neurons have a dual role in CBF increases and decreases, PV neurons are involved in slower CBF increases and that VIP neurons are not involved in CBF regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
different inhibitory neuron sub-types have different roles on CBF regulation and that optogenetic approaches are a powerful tool for investigating these relationships.
the interpretation of brain imaging signals should consider that different neuronal populations have different effects on the regulation of local CBF.
optogenetics can be used to investigate the role of inhibitory neurons in the regulation of CCF and that the results of these experiments may be useful in the interpretation of brain imaging data.
